messages:
liz_docs: Heads-up  I'm assembling a tiny 'cheatsheet' PR for the Optimize toolkit focusing on: batching tunables, prefix cache examples, and migrating old quant keys to q.profile. PR draft: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/1302 :wave:

ben_pm: nice. is this meant for the quickstart or as a separate reference page? we want something short for the release notes.

liz_docs: planning a short reference page + 2 inline snippets that are copy-paste ready. will add a 'quick tuning checklist' so folks can try 3-4 knobs quickly.

sam_eng: please add the per-model fallback example when quant profile isn't supported by a runtime (we still see a few old infra stacks). example: route.policy -> fall back to fp16.

nina_research: also call out perf caveats: quant.profile v2 "aggressive" variants can reduce memory but increase single-token tail latency for seq<32 unless batch_size is lowered. simple perf-run snippet would help.

liz_docs: adding a short bash perf snippet and a minimal Python SDK example. snippet (Python): ```python
from redwood import Client
client = Client(os.getenv('REDWOOD_API_KEY'))
route = {
  "batching": {"batch_size": 4, "max_wait_ms": 25},
  "caching": {"prefix_cache": True, "ttl_seconds": 120},
  "q.profile": "balanced"
}
client.update_route('nlp/assistant', route)
```

sam_eng: tiny nit: use the exact key name 'q.profile' in the config and mention the legacy alias mapping (quant.level -> q.profile) in the migration note.

liz_docs: will add mapping table and a one-liner migration script (sed) to convert legacy YAMLs: ```bash
sed -i 's/quant.level:/q.profile:/g' routes/*.yaml
```

devex: CI link-checker flagged a relative link in the draft referencing /internal/benchmarks. Replace with the canonical public path or add a redirect stub.

doc-bot: spellcheck: 'quantisable' vs 'quantizable' - prefer 'quantizable' per style guide.

nina_research: approved the technical content. left two micro comments about wording in the perf note.

sam_eng: approved.

liz_docs: merged the PR. I'll drop a short blurb in the weekly digest and add a 'how to migrate' section in the Optimize index. Thanks for the quick turn! :rocket:
